name: Bell's Track // Wolfram Creek
description:
Bell's Track // Wolfram Creek [Bike Ride]
Trip leader: Luen Warneke
Date: 9am Sunday 29th October
Location: Paluma Range Resources Reserve, North Queensland, Australia
Distance: ~10 km return
Duration: ~2 hours

Discover the intriguing history of Wolfram mining in the Paluma Range Resources Reserve, where we will ride along old mining tracks and past derelict mines, revealing a fascinating glimpse into North Queensland's past. Please be sure to exercise caution; the mines are no longer stable.
We'll head up the Paluma Range via Mount Spec Road (Paluma Range Road) to Wolfram Creek and take an overgrown road to the left. We will bike along this rough road to explore the historic mine sites. The roads are rough, and we may need to walk our bikes in sections. Expect loose soil and rocks with some steep inclines. Please wear the appropriate safety gear. 

History: The first discovery of tungsten in the area was at Ollera Creek in 1895. Henry Bell and his family established a store and pack horse teams near Ollera Creek in the 1890s. Bell's Track is thought to be named after him. The Wolfram mines peaked in 1905 but were mostly abandoned by 1920 due to a slump in prices.
We urge visitors to respect this historic site. Please do not remove any relics or artefacts; let's keep the area as it is for future generations to appreciate. Take photos (and other people's rubbish) and leave only footprints (and a cleaner environment).

We are meeting at 9 am Sunday 29th Oct at the base of Paluma Range Road (Mount Spec Road) -18.984729, 146.296125

RSVP is required - please contact Luen Warneke at - luenwarneke@gmail.com or sms - 0415947748

What to Bring:
A reliable bike
Helmet
Shoes
2-4 L of drinking water (no reliable water sources)
First aid kit and PLB (Personal Locator Beacon)
Appropriate sun-protective clothing
Sunscreen and insect repellent
Camera

name: Saltwater creek exploration Clemant State Park
description:
Leader: Mitch Nissen 

Description:
Mitch Nissen, is our very own adventure racing legend who has most generously agreed to sharing his knowledge of navigating using a map and compass when in the bush.
This event is a bit of a follow on from the Navigation training course we did with Mitch. At the time we explored some creeklines in the area and our plan is to explore this further using a map and compass. We will plan on exploring a little known waterfall in the area, CP91 - ‘waterfall’ for those that still have their map from last time. 
The aim of the exercise includes: follow the trail using map and compass, walk on a bearing, pace count, learn how to confirm where you are on a map, and identify contour features from the map in real life. 

Numbers - Limited to 15

What to bring:
Come along as if you are heading on a bushwalk - so bring along your morning tea and lunch.
Please wear sun-safe clothing [ Long sleeved shirt/pants as some of the post learning navigation might need us to traverse through long grass and scrub]
Insect repellent. 
Good walking shoes
Water
It is not essential, but a writing pad and pen/pencil to take notes
A compass [available at Anaconda, Tent World or similar stores] if you have one would be good as there might not be enough to go around.
Traditional baseplate for bushwalking: Silva Field Southern Hemisphere Plate Compass | Wildfire Sports & Trek
Thumb compass for navigation racing (orienteering, rogaining) e.g. O-Compass Model 3 Left Handed Southern Hemisphere Thumb Compass | Wildfire Sports & Trek

Meeting Point and Time:
Sent via email
Duration - full day. We will aim to finish by 5 pm.

Fee: non-members/visitors/-  $5 . TBWC Club members - Free. 
You can become a TBWC member after 3 walks as a visitor

https://forms.gle/KsSLgqDoydsvpGbo9

name: Bluegum Circuit - Paluma [mid-week hike]
description:
Leader: Cherry Judge 

Rated: On Track hike. Some creek crossings, Some steep sections. Must be comfortable doing a 4-5+ hr hike . Moderate level fitness required. 

This is a midweek hike for those that are keen to join in.
We will walk the Bluegum Circuit in a clockwise direction, starting along the H-Track.
Along the track we will be taking a detour to visit Triple Falls. Then we continue along the track till we come to a lagoon [on Star River] and then continue along to Miner Creek Falls. From here we start our ascent out of the valley back up to Paluma Village.

What to expect:
- Steep and uneven sections with ropes in place to assist in a couple of places
-Rock hopping & Scrambling.
For more information on the trail and general area, check out the following links:
https://wanderstories.space/bluegum-creek-circuit/
http://paluma.org/

Meeting Point:
6:30 am at  Yabulu Service station, 25km north of Townsville, in the dirt carpark.

RSVP
This event is free for TBWC members
For visitors, it is $5 for insurance cover.
Must be 18+years to attend.

Please RSVP, please email Cherry - info@veteducation.com.au

name: Butterfly Falls canyoning trip
description:
Date: 08/10/23
Leader: Madoc Sheehan	

Madoc will head up Saturday (7th) and stay the night and canyon trip will be Sunday (8th)…9am start at Wallaman falls campground. Can be done even if it rains but nicer in the dry.

Sunday:

We car pool to start of walk (i.e. bridge).

½ - 1 hr: off track walk to start of canyon….lawyer cane, so gloves are nice.  

3-4hr: 2 short (10-15m) free hanging abseils into pools. Requires swim out of 2nd pool (puffed up dry bag helps). Relatively easy entry for abseils and very low to no risk of overhead falling rocks.

2hr: Walk back via butterfly falls track and side-visit to top of birdwing falls.

Drive back to campground…aim for 5pm.  

Suitable for beginner abseilers but must be comfortable with exposure and heights and confident swimmers.

Rope, harnesses, biners and belay devices are sourced from Townsville rockclimbing club for all participants.

Helmets are encouraged. Participants to bring their own.

We have several experienced people in ropework. One to come along who can sit at the bottom of the rope and be the safety backup. 
Madoc will be at the top and make sure everyone is safe and hooked on correctly before they go. We'll have capacity for top belay as well.
We will be tying people in at the top while they wait their turn.

Max participants: 10 (including myself and other experienced canyoners)…8 extras.

We request a bit of detail on your past experience when signing up/showing interest because we’ll vet the group.

Those who have never abseiled before to come up on the Saturday and go through a more straightforward trial run to get some familiarity with what to expect.

For Sunday - Bring: water, lunch, backpack with dry bag, spare clothes for walk out, repellant/sunscreen, gloves.

Register your interest - https://forms.gle/JnV7TRaLSfGaUJv18
